scenes.title: Real transcription, word by word
scenes.narration: This repository demonstrates NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe on a single H one hundred GPU. Three real inference recordings show timed captions: a two-person conversation, a historical speech, and NASA radio.

scenes.title: How the pieces fit
scenes.narration: NeMo Speech and vLLM serve the model. Python scripts submit audio, save responses, verify timing, and build captions. Remotion turns those saved results into short videos.

scenes.title: From WAV to verified result
scenes.narration: A mono wave file enters the transcription request. The saved JSON includes text, word times, speaker tags, and an audio hash. Caption export checks the hash and alignment.

scenes.title: Example: the two-speaker dialogue
scenes.narration: The conversation demo runs thirty-four seconds and has six speaker turns. Its subtitle script groups aligned words by speaker, sentence ending, and pause, making the timeline readable.

scenes.title: Takeaway: traceable captions
scenes.narration: Each clip remains tied to the audio and raw response that produced it. The output is unedited, including errors, so the radio transcript needs listening review before reuse.
